findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (file not found, permission denied, too many open files)
findings.failure_mode: An untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error the caller can handle
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input (e.g. "abc", empty string, or overflow)
findings.failure_mode: A malformed CSV line crashes the program instead of producing a typed parse error the caller can reject
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err() or .checked_cast and return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy narrowing cast from u32. Values in 65536..u32::MAX silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: A legitimate u32 value like 70000 becomes 4448 silently, corrupting data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(u32_val) and return an error on OutOfRange, or use .try_into().map_err()

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexed accesses into a Vec produced by split(',') + collect(). A line with fewer than 2 commas panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.failure_mode: A line like "only_one_field" or an empty line causes a panic, not a recoverable error
findings.fix: Use get(0) and get(1) with Option handling, or use split_once(',') to extract exactly two fields without collecting

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) inside a pure map closure. The function claims to return Vec<Record> but has observable I/O side effects embedded in its data pipeline
findings.failure_mode: Logging is baked into the data transformation, making the function non-deterministic in output, impossible to test without capturing stdout, and impossible to use in a no-logging context
findings.fix: Move println! to the imperative shell (call site). The core function should be a pure calculation with no I/O

findings.problem: split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every line when only two fields are needed. This is the anti-pattern the skill explicitly forbids
findings.failure_mode: Wasteful per-line heap allocations; also means every field is owned even if only the name is used long-term. Using split_once(',') would extract exactly two fields without intermediate allocation
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').map(|(name, value)| ...) to extract exactly two fields with no Vec allocation

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> by value with no bounded allocation. The function does not use try_reserve or any allocation-failure handling before building the collection
findings.failure_mode: A very large file causes an OOM allocation that panics instead of returning a recoverable AllocationError
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, AllocationError>. Use Vec::with_capacity estimated hint plus try_reserve for the real bound, or use a streaming/consumer API

findings.problem: Record uses String for name and u16 for value with no validation at construction. The field is raw u16 with no domain invariants encoded (e.g. non-zero, range-bounded)
findings.failure_mode: Illegal state (zero value, empty name string) is constructable and the compiler cannot prevent it
findings.fix: Use a newtype like NonEmptyName(String) with a fallible constructor, and consider if u16 needs a domain constraint (e.g. checked::NonZeroU16)

findings.problem: No benchmark harness exists. Without benchmarks there is no evidence for any performance claim about load_sessions (e.g. throughput on large files)
findings.failure_mode: Performance regression is undetectable; no baseline to compare against
findings.fix: Add criterion or similar benchmark for load_sessions with realistic input sizes

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or allocation profile
no profiler evidence for per-line allocation patterns
no allocation audit (try_reserve not used anywhere)
no second-ring command evidence (cargo clippy, cargo fmt not run)
no behavior test suite exists to verify error paths
residual_risk: Multiple BLOCKERs: three unwrap() calls (I/O, parse, implicit from .collect() indexing), one lossy narrowing cast (as u16), unchecked indexing into split results, and a hidden println! side effect inside a pure pipeline. The function is not safe for untrusted input or production use. All unwrap() calls and the as cast must be replaced with typed Result propagation before this code can be considered for delivery.
